rationale: 306.7 explicitly notes the removal of the old planeswalker damage-redirection rule, which is exactly why an effect that deals damage only to 'each opponent' can't hit a planeswalker anymore.

508.1d states that if a creature can't attack unless a player pays a cost, that player is not required to pay it, which is why Amelia can decline to pay Ghostly Prison's tax and that creature simply can't attack.

702.37e establishes that turning a face-down permanent up is a special action paying a morph cost, while 118.8 restricts 'additional cost' to spells and abilities being cast/activated; together they show Exiled Doomsayer's tax (a cost increase, not an additional cost) can still be paid with Qarsi Deceiver's restricted mana even though morph is not a spell/ability cast.

109.4a says the controller of a mana ability is determined as though it were on the stack, i.e. by whoever currently controls the source, which is why Moonring Island's mana ability is now controlled by Anabella.

116.2e defines this exact 'discard any time you could cast an instant' effect as a special action, not an activated ability or mana ability, so Phyrexian Revoker's activated-ability lock (naming Channel) doesn't stop it.

729.1b states that effects or definitions created in the main game have no meaning in the subgame except as the subgame-creating effect defines, so Word of Command's 'Nora controls Abraham' doesn't carry into the Shahrazad subgame.

609.4a directly states that if two effects allow the same action 'as though' different conditions were true, both conditions apply, which is why Celestial Dawn's and Thief of Sanity's 'as though' effects both apply to the black mana.

502.3 is the turn-based action of untapping permanents during the untap step, which is the event Undiscovered Paradise's return-to-hand ability is tied to regardless of whether the land itself untaps.

707.2c fixes the copiable values of a copy effect at the moment it first applies, which is why Instigator Gang's back face remains a copy of Ulrich even after transforming; 701.27e then separately governs that a 'transforms into X' trigger checks the object's characteristics immediately after the transform, so the trigger fires.

303.4f requires that when an Aura enters the battlefield other than by resolving as a spell, its controller must choose a legal object or player for it to enchant, which is why Vow of Duty must attach to Deft Duelist and doesn't need a legal target for shroud purposes.

116.2c defines ending a continuous effect as a special action available for as long as the effect exists, meaning Aubrey can't take that action to end Gliding Licid's effect until the ability that creates the effect has actually resolved.

208.3 states a noncreature permanent has no power at all, which is the basis for treating Mirage Mirror's power as not exceeding the threshold once it stops copying Old Man of the Sea, so the control-changing effect keeps applying to Kobolds of Kher Keep.

113.7a is the last-known-information rule: a triggered ability that checks information about its source uses that source's last known information if it's no longer where expected, which is why Paladin of Atonement's life-gain trigger uses its toughness as it existed on the battlefield.

500.7 states extra turns are inserted directly after the specified turn, with the most recently created extra turn taken first, which is the mechanism that fixes where Charlotte's extra turn from Emrakul falls in the turn order relative to Bishop's and Charlotte's normal turns.

614.1 defines replacement effects as watching for a particular event and modifying it regardless of how that event comes about, which is why Uphill Battle's 'creatures enter tapped' effect applies to Dryad Arbor even though it enters via playing a land rather than being cast.

614.4 states replacement effects must exist before the event they modify and can't retroactively apply, so because Solemnity enters at the same instant as Phylactery Lich rather than before it, Solemnity's counter-prevention effect doesn't stop the phylactery counter from being placed on Bronze Sable.

614.4 is the same 'must exist before the event' rule; Suncleanser's counter-prevention effect on Prizefighter Construct already existed before Phylactery Lich entered (unlike the simultaneous case), so it does prevent the counter regardless of when Suncleanser is sacrificed.

614.4 again: Humility enters at the same time as Phylactery Lich, not before it, so Humility's ability-stripping effect can't retroactively have already removed Tatterkite's counter-prevention ability at the moment that mattered.

608.2c states a resolving spell's instructions are followed in the order written, which is why Path to Exile removes Leonin Arbiter (ending its tax) before Nayeli performs the search instructed later on the same card.

603.10a establishes that leaves-the-battlefield triggers look back in time so Slimefoot's dies-trigger fires even though it died simultaneously with its Saproling; 113.7a separately supplies the last-known-information rule used when that trigger resolves and checks whether Slimefoot had lifelink right before dying.

614.4's 'must exist before the event' principle explains why face-down Blightsteel Colossus, having no abilities while on the battlefield, has no replacement effect in place to redirect it to exile instead of the graveyard when it dies.
702.51a scopes convoke's tapping substitution to exactly the colored and generic mana in the spell's total cost, so Ashley cannot tap more of their Soldiers than the total cost actually calls for.

608.2n states a spell is put into the graveyard only as the final part of its resolution, so Beacon Bolt is still on the stack (not yet in the graveyard) while its own damage effect is being calculated.

508.3a explicitly states that 'whenever this attacks' triggers only when a creature is declared as an attacker and specifically will not trigger if the creature is instead put onto the battlefield already attacking, exactly Scourge of the Throne's situation via Kaalia.

701.44b states a permanent 'explores' only after the whole explore process is complete, so Volrath's Shapeshifter already has Nicanzil's text (and thus its trigger condition) in place before the explore event that would satisfy that condition is considered to have happened.

603.10 states that normally objects are checked using their state immediately after an event to see if they match a trigger condition, which is why Blood Operative, already in the graveyard right after the surveil event, is checked there for a surveil-related trigger.

608.2c means Merfolk Trickster's instructions (tap, then lose abilities) happen in the order printed, so Gran-Gran's tap-trigger fires before it loses the ability; 113.7a then separately explains why that already-triggered ability still resolves normally even after its source loses the ability that generated it.

113.6 states abilities of an instant or sorcery function only while it's on the stack, which is why Soulfire Grand Master's lifelink-granting effect doesn't reach Kozilek's Return in the graveyard and why Kozilek's Return's own return-to-hand trigger doesn't function there either.

603.3b lets Ariel choose the order the six simultaneous triggers go on the stack; 608.2d separately establishes that an optional 'may pay' choice on a triggered ability is made as it resolves, not when it's put on the stack, letting Ariel decide to pay only after an untap trigger has already resolved.

603.7d identifies the spell itself as the source of the reflexive/delayed damage trigger Hypothesizzle creates; 113.7a then supplies the last-known-information rule the trigger uses to check whether that source had lifelink, seeing it as it last existed on the stack before Radiant Scrollwielder was cast.

109.5 states that 'you' in an object's text refers to that object's controller at the relevant time, so once Gather Specimens gives Nylah control of Crafty Cutpurse, its own 'create a token' ability creates that token under Nylah, its new controller.

601.2h states unpayable costs can't be paid, and since Dryad Arbor has no mana cost at all (not even {0}) to reference, Illusionary Mask's 'pay mana equal to its mana cost' can never be satisfied for it.

607.2a defines the linked-ability pattern where an exile ability and a second ability referring to 'the exiled cards' are linked, so Phyrexian Ingester's second ability only ever counts the specific creatures its own first ability exiled.

614.10 states that once a turn has started it can no longer be skipped, so the choice to skip Norah's turn (in order to keep Time Vault untapped) must be made before that turn begins, while Norah is still making their own decisions.

608.2h states that an effect requiring information from a specific object uses that object's current information as long as it's in the expected zone, which is why Predict's 'is it named Marble Diamond' check succeeds regardless of the card having just moved to the bottom of the library.

616.1b specifically requires that among competing replacement effects, one that would modify under whose control a permanent enters the battlefield must be chosen before copy-effects are considered, which is why Xantcha's own control-changing ability is applied before Essence of the Wild's copy effect.

110.1 defines a permanent as a card or token on the battlefield, so Pulmonic Sliver's ability (which only affects Sliver permanents) has no effect on Dregscape Sliver once it's a card in the graveyard or being discarded.

The glossary definition of Extra Turn ('a turn created by an effect of a spell or ability') is exactly the category Medomai's restriction keys off, so Medomai can't attack during the extra turn Savor the Moment grants regardless of what specifically restricts that turn.

608.2c means Austere Command's chosen modes resolve in the order printed on the card; 701.19a separately establishes that an activated regeneration shield protects a permanent only the next time it would be destroyed that turn, so once used up on the artifact-destroying mode it's gone for the creature-destroying mode.

115.1 defines what it means for something to be a target of a spell or ability, establishing that Spellskite's activated ability targets Fiery Impulse itself (the spell), not Spellskite, so Spellskite doesn't become a target again and Venerated Rotpriest triggers only once.

616.1 states that when multiple replacement effects would modify the same event, the affected object's controller chooses which to apply, which is why Amaya (Dralnu's controller) gets to pick the order between Dralnu, Lich Lord's and Furnace of Rath's competing damage-replacement effects.

707.2c fixes Metamorphic Alteration's copiable values (Village Ironsmith's front face) at the moment the copy effect first applies, so later changes to Village Ironsmith don't update Colossapede; 712.9 separately states only permanents represented by double-faced cards/tokens can transform, so Colossapede itself never transforms.

121.2d lets the active team choose the order its members draw during the shared draw step, so the partner can draw first; 810.5 separately confirms teammates may review each other's hands at any time, so Arturo can see and consider that already-drawn card before making Underrealm Lich's choice.

608.2b requires targets to be rechecked for legality as a spell or ability resolves, which is why Siren Stormtamer's own ability (which can only target a spell that targets Nevaeh or her permanent) fails to still qualify once Stormtamer itself has been sacrificed, letting Explosion resolve and Alex draw his cards.

702.7c explicitly states that removing first strike from a creature after it has already dealt first-strike combat damage does not let it also deal damage in the regular combat damage step, exactly Elvish Archers's situation after Turn to Frog.

608.2d states that choices offered by a resolving effect (such as each player's choice of which permanent to put onto the battlefield via Show and Tell) are announced as the effect is applied, which is why both cards are revealed to both players before either player's own entering-battlefield choice, like Hall of Triumph's creature type, is made.

601.2b explicitly states a player can't apply two alternative methods of casting or two alternative costs to a single spell, so having already chosen flashback (Snapcaster Mage's granted alternative cost) to cast Nourishing Shoal from the graveyard, Nevaeh can't also use its own life-payment alternative cost.

701.3b states that attaching an Aura, Equipment, or Fortification to the object it's already attached to does nothing, so re-equipping Fleetfeather Sandals onto Wandering Ones doesn't give it a new timestamp; 613.7 separately establishes that within a layer, the effect with the later timestamp is applied last, so Tightening Coils (still the more recent timestamp) wins and removes flying.

103.5 establishes mulligan declarations happen in turn order (starting player first, then others), so Albert's declaration slot can come before Nico's; 103.5b separately states that using an ability like Serum Powder's happens exactly at the moment that player would declare a mulligan, which for Albert falls before Nico has had to decide.

103.6 states opening-hand actions like putting Leyline of Punishment onto the battlefield happen only once the mulligan process is entirely complete; 103.5b separately ties Serum Powder's usable window to 'any time you could mulligan,' a window that has already closed by the time Leyline's opening-hand action is taken.
